course.title: Advanced Modelling for Structured Data
course.tagline: Decide when pretrained models, stacked ensembles and decision-aware pipelines earn their place, measured against tuned baselines and under shift
course.description: Participants decide when pretrained models, ensembles and decision-aware pipelines earn their place in structured-data work. On a fictional food wholesaler's synthetic orders and demand, they test pretrained tabular models and zero-shot forecasters against tuned baselines, stack ensembles, turn forecasts into orders by optimisation, score models by decision cost and validate under the shift of a new depot region. They end with an adoption decision weighing accuracy, licence, cost and data residency.
course.audience: Specialists. Data scientists who have completed the level 300 core or can show equivalent work: a defended analysis with a validated model or a causal estimate that they can explain.
prerequisites: DS-305 Uncertainty, Interpretability and Model Validation
Formulates a simple linear programme, or completes the pre-work

Setup: a laptop CPU with uv, or Google Colab. No key and no model download is needed on a laptop: the pretrained models run in a Colab runtime, and a labelled stand-in answers elsewhere. Run 00_setup_check before Day 1; see labs/README.md.
course.format_note: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task

outcomes.text: Evaluate a pretrained tabular model against a tuned, ensembled boosted-tree baseline across training-set sizes, given late-delivery records from 500 to 50,000 orders and a fixed compute budget
outcomes.evidence: learning curves with intervals showing where each approach wins

outcomes.text: Evaluate zero-shot pretrained forecasters, with and without covariates, against statistical and tuned learned benchmarks by rolling-origin backtests, given 400 demand series with Hijri holiday covariates
outcomes.evidence: point and quantile accuracy by series group

outcomes.text: Implement a stacked ensemble from out-of-fold or rolling-origin predictions and measure its improvement over the best single model, given four fitted candidate models
outcomes.evidence: a stacking run with the improvement and its interval

outcomes.text: Build a predict-then-optimise pipeline and judge forecasters by the decision cost they cause, given capacity limits, holding costs and shortage costs
outcomes.evidence: regret per forecaster compared with the error ranking

outcomes.text: Diagnose distribution shift between training and deployment data and validate a model under it, given a new depot region and a holiday season that moves between years
outcomes.evidence: a shift report with adversarial, grouped and temporal validation and a corrected error estimate

outcomes.text: Decide whether to adopt a pretrained model for one task, weighing accuracy, cost, licence and data residency, given two candidate models, their licences and the wholesaler's data classification
outcomes.evidence: a defended adoption memo with a reusable evaluation protocol

case_study.name: Bustan Food Wholesale
case_study.summary: Bustan Food Wholesale is a fictional food wholesaler with depots in Riyadh, Buraidah, Jeddah and Dammam and a new northern region around Hail and Tabuk. Participants test a pretrained tabular model against a tuned boosted-tree baseline on 80,000 orders, score zero-shot forecasters with and without Ramadan and Eid covariates on 400 daily demand series over three Hijri years, stack forecasters, turn forecasts into orders and truck plans by optimisation, rank forecasters by the regret they cause, validate a model under the shift of the new region and end with an adoption decision on licence, cost and data residency. All data is synthetic and generated with a fixed seed.

days.label: Capstone
days.title: Capstone project presentations
days.subtitle: An evaluation protocol and an adoption decision, defended before two assessors

capstone.summary: An evaluation protocol and adoption decision for one structured-data task (two pretrained candidates, a tuned baseline, an ensemble, validation under a stated shift, regret where relevant) in a public repository whose README reports measured results; defence before two assessors
capstone.submission: A public GitHub repository link: the evaluation protocol run end to end (two pretrained candidates, a tuned baseline, an ensemble, validation under a stated shift, regret where a decision follows), a README that reports the measured results with intervals and the adoption decision with its conditions, the run logs and a verification note on AI-assisted steps. Then a defence before two assessors: one assessor names a new shift scenario and the participant predicts which validation result changes before re-running it.
